newsitem.title: UK: Jamaica's first Eurobond sees spread tighten 40 bp.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica's first Eurobond sees spread tighten 40 bp.

text.p: Jamaica's first Eurobond saw such strong demand that the spread tightened more than 40 basis points when the deal was freed to trade, bankers said on Thursday.
The order book was also so big and broad-based that lead managers Bankers Trust were able to raise double the amount initially intended.
"The quality of the book is excellent and we had a very positive reaction," Bankers Trust syndicate manager said.
The $200 million five-year bond -- which was five times oversubscribed -- was priced to yield 335 basis points over the when-issued five-year U.S. Treasury due 2002.
The spread tightened to 290 b.p. in secondary market trade, although Bankers Trust expected the spread to widen out a bit after the initial run.
"The rapid tightening was due to people trying to get bonds on a hot deal," he said.
Bankers Trust said the reasons the bond had sold so well was Jamaica's positive economic story.
Although the country is unrated it did not inhibit demand, the syndicate manager said.
"(A rating) is something the country is considering," he said.
Added to this he said the yield pick-up was attractive relative to other Latin American borrowers as current launch spreads had tightened a lot.
"Investors are asking were the value is," he said.
The government said it intends to use the funds raised to reduce the cost of servicing domestic debt.
